% Written by `lab paper tactic-found`; do not edit by hand.
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{lL}
\toprule
Feature & What it counts \\
\midrule
\texttt{material\_count} & Both sides' material added up, a pawn as 1, a knight 3, a bishop 3.25, a rook 5, a queen 9. \\
\texttt{material\_imbalance} & The mover's material less the opponent's, on the same scale. \\
\texttt{phase\_piece\_count} & Knights, bishops, rooks and queens still on the board, both sides. \\
\texttt{in\_check} & Whether the mover is in check. \\
\texttt{legal\_moves} & How many legal moves the mover has. \\
\texttt{legal\_captures} & How many of the mover's legal moves take something. \\
\texttt{legal\_checks} & How many of the mover's legal moves give check. \\
\texttt{hanging\_own} & The mover's pieces that something cheaper attacks, or that anything attacks while nothing defends them. \\
\texttt{hanging\_opponent} & The opponent's pieces that something cheaper attacks, or that anything attacks while nothing defends them. \\
\texttt{passed\_pawns\_own} & The mover's pawns with no enemy pawn ahead of them on their file or a neighbouring one. \\
\texttt{passed\_pawns\_opponent} & The opponent's pawns with no enemy pawn ahead of them on their file or a neighbouring one. \\
\texttt{attackers\_near\_own\_king} & How many attacks the opponent has on the squares around the mover's king. \\
\texttt{attackers\_near\_opponent\_king} & How many attacks the mover has on the squares around the opponent's king. \\
\texttt{first\_piece} & Which piece makes the line's first move, from pawn (1) to king (6). \\
\texttt{first\_capture} & Whether the line's first move takes something. \\
\texttt{first\_captured\_value} & The value of what the line's first move takes. \\
\texttt{first\_check} & Whether the line's first move gives check. \\
\texttt{first\_promotion} & Whether the line's first move promotes a pawn. \\
\texttt{first\_distance} & How many squares the first move travels, counted as a king would walk it. \\
\texttt{first\_backward} & Whether the first move goes back toward the mover's own side. \\
\texttt{first\_to\_attacked} & Whether the opponent attacks the square the first move lands on. \\
\texttt{first\_sacrifice} & Whether the piece that moves first can be taken where it lands, having won less than it is worth. \\
\texttt{line\_checks} & How many of the solver's moves give check. \\
\texttt{line\_captures} & How many of the solver's moves take something. \\
\texttt{line\_quiet} & How many of the solver's moves neither take nor check. \\
\texttt{line\_promotions} & How many of the solver's moves promote a pawn. \\
\texttt{line\_pieces\_moved} & How many different pieces the solver moves. \\
\texttt{line\_sacrifices} & How many of the solver's moves give up material. \\
\texttt{line\_max\_distance} & The longest distance one of the solver's moves travels. \\
\texttt{ends\_in\_mate} & Whether the line ends in checkmate. \\
\texttt{reply\_captures} & How many of the opponent's replies in the line take something. \\
\texttt{setup\_capture} & Whether the opponent's move that set the position up took something. \\
\texttt{final\_material\_gain} & The material balance after the line, less the balance before it. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
